day_shape: 57 items: IRGC claims destruction of three F-35s at Jordan's Al-Azraq and hits on Al-Asad, CENTCOM says it struck dozens of IRGC targets in Iran, Araghchi protests to Bulgaria and Cyprus over base use, nothing from UK Parliament or OFAC.

threads.label: US-Iran direct strikes exchange
threads.summary: US Central Command said it carried out a heavy wave of strikes on dozens of IRGC targets inside Iran early Thursday, a day after Iranian ballistic missile fire on US regional forces. The IRGC's Statement 55 claimed complete destruction of three F-35s and heavy damage to three more at Al-Azraq base in Jordan, plus two drone hangars and a fuel tank at Al-Asad; the Jerusalem Post relayed the IRGC claim.

threads.label: Iranian protests over third-country bases
threads.summary: Foreign Minister Araghchi told Bulgaria's foreign minister that hosting US military aircraft at Bozhurishte Air Base violated the UN Charter, and told Cyprus's Constantinos Kombos to prevent misuse of foreign bases against Iran. Defa Press and IRIB carried both readouts.

threads.label: Regional spillover: Yemen, Iraq, Egypt, Saudi
threads.summary: The Jerusalem Post reported strikes in Iraq and Egypt after the Houthis' declared naval blockade on Saudi Arabia, and cited a NYT report attributing a US tanker explosion at Egypt's Damietta port to an Iranian drone. Houthi leader Abdulmalik al-Houthi called US and Saudi strikes on Iraq 'treacherous', Yemen's foreign ministry denied attacking Egypt, and Iraq's armed forces spokesman said there was no evidence of attacks from Iraqi territory on Saudi Arabia.

threads.label: Gaza operations and Cairo track
threads.summary: The IDF said it struck four more Hamas weapons depots overnight in Gaza and announced the killing of Hamas sniper cell commander Ahmad Hisham Mahmoud Louh and October 7 infiltrator Mahmoud Ali Mahmoud Taroush. The Jerusalem Post reported Cairo talks advancing on a roadmap requiring full Hamas disarmament, tunnel dismantling and no governing or military role for the group.

threads.label: Domestic repression reporting
threads.summary: Iran International reported that three political prisoners in Evin issued a joint statement accusing authorities of using the regional war as cover to escalate executions, and separately reported security agents cut royalist tattoos from a 21-year-old protester before shooting him. A third piece described municipal crews demolishing cafe seating on Tehran's Sanaei Street.

events.title_en: Mass exodus of over 100 Israeli soldiers from barracks and laying down of weapons
events.summary_en: Mass exodus of over 100 Israeli soldiers from barracks and laying down of weapons. According to Israeli media Yisrael Hayom, an unusual incident occurred in the Israeli army on Thursday: dozens of troops and several commanders from a battalion of the Givaati Brigade left the Sde Timan barracks without permission and effectively went AWOL (absent without leave). The report states that this action appeared to be somewhat coordinated and initial figures indicate participation of over 100 people. According to details released, the situation escalated after a verbal altercation and tension with the battalion commander; the commander allegedly removed some symbolic boards and morale-boosting slogans of the unit that were important to the troops.

events.title_en: War against Iran caused severe decline in Saudi Arabia's economic growth
events.summary_en: War against Iran caused severe decline in Saudi Arabia's economic growth. Bloomberg reported that Saudi Arabia's gross domestic product in the second quarter of the current calendar year declined 4.8 per cent compared to the same period of the previous year. This comes as the country had experienced three per cent growth in the first quarter of the current calendar year. A decline of around 25 per cent in oil production was cited as the main factor in Saudi Arabia's economic stagnation. Bloomberg wrote that the war by the United States and the Zionist regime against Iran has placed heavy pressure on Saudi Arabia's economy and disruption in the passage of oil tankers through the Strait of Hormuz and the decline in oil exports has affected Riyadh's oil revenues.
